title: Ada
subtitle: The language built for software that must not fail, taught as modern Ada 2012 and Ada 2022: strong types, packages, contracts, tasking and a first look at formal proof with SPARK.
description: Ada is a compiled, strongly typed language designed for the United States Department of Defense by a team led by Jean Ichbiah. Its first reference manual appeared in 1980, and it became an ANSI standard, Ada 83, in 1983; it has been revised as Ada 95, Ada 2005, Ada 2012 and Ada 2022. It is used where a software failure can cost lives or fortunes: flight-control and avionics software, railway signalling, air-traffic control, satellites and launchers, defence systems and, increasingly, security-critical firmware. Its signature ideas are types that model the problem exactly, packages that hide what should be hidden, contracts that state what code promises, concurrency built into the language, and SPARK, a subset of Ada whose programs can be proved free of whole classes of errors.

This course teaches **modern Ada**: Ada 2012, with the Ada 2022 features that the GNAT 14 compiler supports, marked as such. It goes from a first program, through types, subprograms, records, arrays and strings, packages and generics, to object orientation with tagged types, contracts, tasks and protected objects, and ends with a complete concurrent project. It assumes the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are. No previous Ada is needed.

To run the programs you need the GNAT compiler. The Ada community recommends installing it with [Alire](https://alire.ada.dev/), Ada's package manager, which downloads a toolchain for Linux, macOS or Windows (see [Getting started on ada-lang.io](https://ada-lang.io/docs/learn/getting-started/installation)); on Debian and Ubuntu, `sudo apt install gnat gprbuild` also works. There is no official online playground, but the interactive courses at [learn.adacore.com](https://learn.adacore.com/) let you edit and run Ada in the browser. Every program in this course was compiled and run with GNAT 14.

levels.title: The core language
levels.summary: Where Ada came from and how to compile it, the strong types, ranges and subtypes at its heart, control flow, and procedures and functions with their parameter modes and exceptions.

levels.title: Data and abstraction
levels.summary: Records, arrays and strings for modelling data, packages and generics for building abstractions that hide their details, and tagged types for object-oriented design.

levels.title: Ada for high-integrity software
levels.summary: Contracts, predicates and invariants with an overview of SPARK proof, then tasks and protected objects for concurrency, the Alire workflow and a complete project.
